# Campaign planning reference

Load this when choosing channels, building a calendar or setting metrics. Benchmarks are rough starting points; replace them with the company's own history when it exists.

## Five-part framework

Every campaign rests on: **objective, audience, message, channel, measure**.

| Objective | Measured by |
| --- | --- |
| Awareness | Reach, impressions, share of voice, direct traffic |
| Consideration | Content engagement, signups, webinar attendance |
| Conversion | Leads, demos, purchases, pipeline |
| Retention | Churn change, upsell, satisfaction scores |
| Advocacy | Referrals, reviews, user-generated content |

Write objectives as Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound. Example: "200 qualified leads from mid-size logistics firms in 6 weeks."

Audience profile in one sentence: "[Role] at [company type] struggling with [pain] and looking for [outcome]. They find solutions through [channels] and care most about [priorities]."

Message hierarchy: why should I care, what is the solution, why you, what should I do now. Each supporting message needs a proof point (data, case study, testimonial, third-party validation).

## Channel guide

| Type | Channel | Best for | Typical metrics | Effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Owned | Website or blog | Search, education, thought leadership | Traffic, conversions | Medium |
| Owned | Email | Nurture, retention, announcements | Open rate, click rate, conversions | Low to medium |
| Owned | Organic social | Awareness, community | Engagement, reach, follower growth | Medium |
| Owned | Webinars, podcast | Education, lead generation | Registrations, attendance, pipeline | High |
| Earned | PR and media | Credibility, launches | Coverage, referral traffic | High |
| Earned | Guest content, partners | Audience expansion | Referral traffic, backlinks | Medium |
| Earned | Community, reviews | Trust, consideration | Mentions, review volume and rating | Low to medium |
| Paid | Search ads | High-intent demand capture | Cost per click, conversion rate, cost per acquisition | Medium |
| Paid | Social ads | Awareness, retargeting, lead generation | Cost per thousand views, click rate, cost per acquisition | Medium |
| Paid | Sponsored content, events | Thought leadership, relationships | Leads, meetings, pipeline influenced | Medium to high |

Selection questions: where does the audience spend time, which buying stage is targeted, what budget exists (paid needs money, owned and earned need time), which assets already exist, what worked before.

## Calendar building

1. Start with fixed milestones (launch date, event, season).
2. Work backward using production lead times.
3. Cover awareness, consideration and conversion content.
4. Group pieces into weekly themes.
5. Spread across channels so the audience meets the campaign more than once.
6. Leave about 20% of slots open for reactive content.

Typical production lead times: blog post 3-5 business days, email 2-3, social posts 1-2, landing page 5-7, video 2-4 weeks, long report or e-book 2-4 weeks.

## Budget starting points

| Category | Share of budget |
| --- | --- |
| Paid acquisition | 30-40% |
| Content production | 20-30% |
| Events and sponsorships | 10-20% |
| Tools | 10-15% |
| Experiments | 5-10% |

Put most paid spend (about 60-70%) on the highest-confidence channel, keep 15-20% for tests, review monthly and add 10-15% contingency. Always include production cost, not only media spend.

## Metrics by campaign type

| Campaign | Primary metrics |
| --- | --- |
| Awareness | Reach, brand mentions, share of voice, direct traffic |
| Lead generation | Leads, qualified leads, cost per lead, pipeline influenced |
| Product launch | Signups or trials, activation rate, coverage, feature adoption |
| Retention | Churn change, engagement, satisfaction, expansion revenue |
| Event or webinar | Registrations, attendance rate, post-event conversions |

## Plan-level principles

- Treat marketing as a portfolio of compounding assets (search content, an email list, a community, a referral loop) rather than one-off spikes.
- No single tactic fixes growth. Many small, measured moves do.
- Every move names its mechanism and a leading indicator. A move that cannot be measured becomes an experiment with a stop rule.
- Split effort roughly 70% current channels, 20% next channel, 10% experiments, so the next channel is funded before the current one plateaus.
